editorial.title: Capacity Exists, But How Much Can I Use Now?
editorial.dek: The global container fleet is bigger than ever. Yet effective capacity is shrinking.
body: The global container fleet is bigger than ever. There are ships in the water, containers in circulation and terminals operating. Yet effective capacity is shrinking.

Current port congestion is a useful example. More than 4.3 million TEU of container capacity is reportedly waiting to berth worldwide, exceeding the absolute congestion peak seen during the pandemic. East Asia is carrying much of that pressure, with large queues at Shanghai and Ningbo. Vessel delays are increasingly measured in days rather than hours.

A 15,000-TEU vessel sitting outside a port is still technically part of the global fleet. But while it waits, the ship falls behind schedule. Its next port call moves. Containers miss connections. Equipment stays in the wrong place. Another service begins operating with less usable capacity.

A major carrier has omitted a Shanghai call on one service after adverse weather affected the schedule, rerouting cargo to protect the onward rotation. That makes operational sense for the vessel, but the affected containers now require another solution.
What actually matters is usable capacity at the time and place where the cargo needs it.
Congestion, weather, security, equipment imbalance, missed connections and specialized cargo requirements all consume usable capacity.
The transportation asset does not have to disappear. It only has to stop being available when you need it.
The question, then, is not simply:
“How much capacity can I actually use, reliably, right now?”

items.title: Shipping traffic via Strait of Hormuz slips below 10-day average, data shows
items.discovery: Middle East chokepoint and energy-shipping scan
items.summary: Visible commodity-vessel traffic through Hormuz fell to seven transits on August 27 from 17 a day earlier, below the recent 10-day average of 15, according to preliminary Kpler data cited by Reuters. Counts can change because some vessels may operate without normal AIS visibility.
items.logisticsImpact: The renewed drop shows that physical access has not translated into dependable capacity. Gulf operators still face unstable sailing patterns, insurance exposure, security risk and uncertain energy-shipping schedules despite diplomatic efforts around the waterway.

items.title: Typhoon Saudel shuts China’s Ningbo terminals as Hapag-Lloyd warns of 11-day Shanghai waits
items.discovery: East Asia port and severe-weather scan
items.summary: Ningbo-Zhoushan container terminals halted operations as Typhoon Saudel approached, with 55 large container vessels moved to shelter. Hapag-Lloyd’s latest congestion update cited Shanghai Yangshan waits of up to 11 days and Ningbo waits of three to six days.
items.logisticsImpact: A fresh terminal shutdown on top of severe Shanghai-Ningbo queues can push vessel rotations further off schedule, deepen equipment imbalance and disrupt Asia-Europe and transpacific connections.

items.title: As war strands Qatari gas for 6 months, US sales rise and European stocks plummet
items.summary: Qatar exported only 18 LNG cargoes over six months, down from 509 in the comparable period a year earlier, Reuters reported. Before the conflict, Qatar supplied about one-fifth of global daily LNG, while U.S. exports have risen as Europe enters the storage season with tighter inventories.
items.logisticsImpact: The loss of Qatari LNG is reshaping long-haul vessel demand, sourcing and destination patterns while increasing exposure to U.S. export capacity, European storage constraints and elevated gas prices.

items.title: MSC halts bookings at Russia’s Novorossiysk after drone hits containership
items.discovery: Black Sea security and carrier-operations scan
items.summary: MSC suspended new cargo bookings to and from Novorossiysk after the containership MSC ULSAN III was hit by a drone while approaching the Russian Black Sea port. The carrier said weekly service could resume subject to security conditions.
items.logisticsImpact: Booking suspension removes a major liner option at a key Russian gateway and can force cargo into alternative ports, routes or storage while security conditions remain unstable.

items.title: SK Gas pays record $5.3m to jump Panama Canal queue
items.summary: SK Gas reportedly paid $5.3 million for an expedited Panama Canal slot for LPG carrier G. Spirit, as low rainfall tightens transit access. The canal has announced capacity reductions beginning in September, while ships without reservations can face waits of around 11 days.
items.logisticsImpact: Scarcer canal slots are turning schedule certainty into a premium service. LPG, container and other operators face higher auction costs, longer waits or diversion decisions as freshwater constraints reduce daily transit capacity.

items.title: Exporturile de cereale ale Ucrainei sunt încetinite de lipsa piloţilor care să treacă navele pe Canalul Sulina
items.discovery: Romanian-language Danube and Ukraine export scan
items.summary: About 70 vessels were waiting near Romania’s Sulina Canal for access to Ukrainian Danube ports. Pilot shortages, priority for fuel cargoes, air-raid alerts and weather have reduced effective passage toward Ukrainian ports to roughly two or three vessels a day.
items.logisticsImpact: The Danube fallback route is becoming its own bottleneck. Grain exporters face vessel queues, demurrage exposure and weaker export throughput while Black Sea alternatives remain constrained by security risk.

items.title: New crisis at Durban port prompts calls for urgent action
items.discovery: Southern Africa port and landside-operations scan
items.summary: Durban Gateway Terminal delays have worsened, with anchorage waits near seven days and berth time close to five days. South African freight groups say throughput fell after a terminal-system migration, while equipment, yard and truck congestion are compounding the disruption.
items.logisticsImpact: Durban’s deterioration is affecting vessel schedules, container evacuation and truck productivity at South Africa’s largest container gateway, while storage, detention and demurrage costs are spreading through import and manufacturing supply chains.

items.title: Gulf crisis sees Jebel Ali crash out of top 30 box port ranks after 20 years
items.discovery: Middle East container-gateway and network-shift scan
items.summary: Alphaliner data reported by The Loadstar shows Jebel Ali handled 3.14 million TEU in the first half, down from 7.77 million a year earlier, dropping from 10th to 32nd globally. Colombo and Nhava Sheva gained traffic as carriers sought alternatives to Gulf routings.
items.logisticsImpact: The volume shift illustrates how prolonged Gulf disruption is redrawing transshipment patterns, concentrating more cargo on South Asian alternatives and changing feeder, equipment and mainline network requirements.

items.title: Prince Rupert opens rail-linked CANXPORT export logistics hub
items.discovery: North American port infrastructure and export-logistics scan
items.summary: The Port of Prince Rupert has opened CANXPORT, a rail-linked export logistics facility designed to handle at least 400,000 shipping containers annually, with expansion potential to 750,000. The facility includes dedicated inbound and outbound rail tracks plus road infrastructure for export transloading.
items.logisticsImpact: CANXPORT adds intermodal export capacity at a key Pacific gateway and can improve rail-to-vessel flows for Canadian forestry products, agricultural commodities and resins while giving shippers more routing flexibility through Prince Rupert.

items.title: Port of Tauranga reports record underlying profit as productivity continues to improve
items.discovery: Oceania port capacity and infrastructure scan
items.summary: New Zealand’s largest port said its container terminal is effectively at capacity and unable to accommodate new shipping services. Container throughput still rose 0.4% to 1.21 million TEU, while berth constraints contributed to a 5.5% decline in transshipment volumes for the year ended June 30.
items.logisticsImpact: Tauranga’s berth constraint limits New Zealand’s ability to absorb new liner services or vessel bunching. Until expansion advances, importers and exporters face reduced routing flexibility even as terminal productivity improves.

items.title: S. Korea seeks to accelerate green transition in shipping under new blueprint
items.discovery: East Asia maritime-policy and fleet-transition scan
items.summary: South Korea unveiled a 2026–2035 plan to support the transition of 889 public and private vessels to eco-friendly models. The government says the program is intended to cut emissions while strengthening domestic shipping and shipbuilding competitiveness.
items.logisticsImpact: Fleet-transition support can accelerate demand for alternative-fuel vessels, retrofits and port-fueling infrastructure, while adding capital and technology decisions for operators trading through Korean ports.

items.title: ADB Approves $400 Million Financing Facility to Modernize Borders, Facilitate Trade in CAREC Region
items.discovery: Central Asia border, customs and trade-facilitation scan
items.summary: ADB approved a $400 million financing facility aimed at modernizing border infrastructure and trade processes across the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation corridor. The program is designed to improve cross-border movement and reduce trade friction in participating economies.
items.logisticsImpact: Better border facilities and processing can reduce truck and cargo dwell times across CAREC corridors, improving overland reliability between Central Asia, the Caucasus and wider Eurasian trade routes.

items.title: Newport rail line disrupted after freight train derails
items.summary: A diesel freight train derailed near Newport in Melbourne, disrupting the Newport–Sunshine freight line, a key connection toward Adelaide and onward interstate corridors. Trains required rerouting while crews assessed track damage. No major injury was reported in available coverage.
items.logisticsImpact: Even a localized derailment can constrain paths through a critical Melbourne freight junction, forcing reroutes and creating knock-on timing risk for interstate rail freight while infrastructure is inspected and repaired.

items.title: Air China Cargo partners with cargo.one to debut e-booking for thousands of freight forwarders
items.discovery: Global air-cargo carrier and digital-booking scan
items.summary: Air China Cargo has made capacity available through cargo.one in its first global digital distribution partnership, initially opening e-booking access on key trade lanes from Europe and North America to China and beyond. The carrier combines a 24-freighter fleet with belly capacity across Air China’s passenger network.
items.logisticsImpact: Forwarders gain faster digital access to Air China Cargo pricing and capacity, reducing manual booking friction and broadening electronic procurement options on China-linked airfreight lanes.
